# Korve documentation

Korve is an agent-era application platform. Build with an agent, deploy from Git, and operate apps,
databases, storage, queues, crons, caches, observability, budgets, and recovery through one public
contract.

Canonical docs: https://docs.korve.dev
Dashboard and product: https://korve.dev
API base: https://api.korve.dev
OpenAPI 3.1: https://api.korve.dev/v1/spec
MCP Code Mode: https://mcp.korve.dev/mcp

Start:
- https://docs.korve.dev/introduction
- https://docs.korve.dev/quickstart
- https://docs.korve.dev/agents/agent-onboarding
- https://docs.korve.dev/agents/mcp-setup
- https://docs.korve.dev/agents/oauth
- https://docs.korve.dev/primitives/app-access
- https://docs.korve.dev/primitives/project-operator
- https://docs.korve.dev/primitives/project-maintenance
- https://docs.korve.dev/primitives/manifests
- https://docs.korve.dev/api-reference/overview

Rules for agents:
- Search the public contract before building or mutating infrastructure.
- Use organization API keys only for operator automation; never ship them in customer applications.
- Read current state, plan multi-resource changes, ask approval for dangerous/destructive actions,
  then verify the resulting state.
- Treat shown-once secrets as secrets and exported ******** values as preserve-live-value markers.
- Queue delivery is at least once; make durable side effects idempotent.
- Do not assume region or metric ids. Discover them from the current regions and metrics catalogs.
- CLI and MCP OAuth grants are audience-bound; never reuse a CLI token for MCP.
- A protected app-access policy is safe to activate only when enforcement reports ready.
- Operator and maintenance mutations are persisted, version-bound actions; a signed-in human must
  decide elevated actions, and execution must be verified before it is called successful.
